answer: To resist Sybil attacks, an agent economy can require every new identity to burn a small but real amount of tokens at registration, a sunk cost that never returns. Honest operators pay it once; an attacker spawning a thousand fake identities must pay it a thousand times, making mass fabrication uneconomical. Verified identities then form a haven of peers whose long transaction history grows like a garden, accumulating reputation roots over time, while cheap fakes remain saplings and lack the ivory-hard credentials only earned through honest participation.
